title: 32.6 A Dynamic-RON-Diminished Bidirectional GaN Load Switch with Inrush Current Protection and Spike Attenuation
problem: Bidirectional GaN load switches for 48V EV power systems require both reverse-current blocking and bidirectional current transfer; monolithic bidirectional GaN (Bi-GaN) devices reduce on-resistance vs. discrete back-to-back solutions but suffer from overstress during turn-off when gate-to-source voltage exceeds breakdown limits, requiring complex turn-off selectors.
motivation: 48V EV battery management requires efficient and safe bidirectional power switching; minimizing on-resistance losses reduces heat dissipation and battery depletion rates.
method: The design combines a single integrated GaN transistor with a control system that can route its input signal through either of two paths. When the switch turns off, the device automatically selects the path that keeps the control voltage within safe limits, preventing damage. It also includes built-in circuits for inrush current protection (limiting the sudden surge when turning on) and spike attenuation (smoothing voltage transients during switching).
key_novelty: The core innovation is automatically choosing between control paths to prevent device damage during turn-off, with all the protection built into a single GaN chip instead of relying on external control circuits.
contributions: Dynamic gate-to-source voltage control strategy preventing overstress during turn-off
Monolithic Bi-GaN CD topology achieving 38% area reduction vs. discrete back-to-back
Integrated inrush-current protection for battery charger safety
Spike-attenuation circuitry reducing EMI and ringing on load-switch transitions
limitations: Specific on-resistance values, power loss, and inrush-current limit thresholds not provided in abstract.
primary_theme: Bidirectional GaN load switch with dynamic RON control for 48V EV power systems
